title: Path Sum
prompt:
Given the `root` of a binary tree and an integer `targetSum`, return `true` if the tree has a root-to-leaf path such that adding up all the values along the path equals `targetSum`, or `false` otherwise.

A leaf is a node with no children. The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array and `targetSum`; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from the array, so you only need to implement the path check.

examples.explanation: No root-to-leaf path (1->2 sums to 3, 1->3 sums to 4) equals 5.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 5000]
hints: As you recurse down, subtract the current node's value from the remaining target so each call only needs to check whether the remainder matches a leaf's value.
A node only counts as a valid ending point if it's a leaf (no left and no right child) — an internal node hitting sum zero doesn't count.
Base case: an empty tree can never satisfy a path sum, so it returns false immediately regardless of the remaining target.

solution.approach: Recursively walk down from the root, subtracting each node's value from the remaining target. At a leaf, the path is valid only if the remaining target after subtracting the leaf's value is exactly zero. For an internal node, the path exists if either subtree (with the updated remaining sum) has a valid path. An empty tree never has a valid path.
